items.title: Harry Shields Interview, 1961-05-28
items.q: Larry told me that... He said they were working at the Casino Gardens in Chicago... Larry says, and Nick said, sounds good.

ctx.x: You know, Nick LaRocca makes a big point that it all started with the original Dixieland and there was not anything you could call jazz before that. Of course they probably were the first ones to use that name.

They were the first ones to use that name. Larry told me that. He said that's true. Now Larry was very truthful. I never knew of Larry to ever tell a lie. He told me that. He said they were working at the Casino Gardens in Chicago. And the band was going pretty good. And they were getting a real good salary of $35 a week then. You see. So that was in 1915 or 16. And some fella come in and said, Jazz are up. You know, he said he was half loaded. So they said, huh? What was that? He said, Jazz. That's Jazz are up,…
The first records they have had that. J-A-S.
